newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to float Bank Leumi shares.
newsitem.headline: Israel to float Bank Leumi shares.

text.p: Israel's government will offer stock and warrants next week in Bank Leumi, marking a major step forward in its effort to speed up privatisation of the country's banks.

After a successful pre-sale of shares to foreign institutions, underwriters said Wednesday they were boosting the size of the public offering, set for May 27, by $25 million to a total of $150 million, or 14 percent of the bank's equity.
Earlier in the week, about 20 European institutional investors pre-commmitted to purchasing $120 million worth of shares and warrants at a minimum price of 5 shekels each ($1.47).
The Israeli government now controls 82 percent of Leumi, with the remainder traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

This year has seen a flurry of action in Israel's nearly moribund bank-privatisation programme. The government has controlling stakes in four of the country's five biggest banks, which it acquired after bailing out shareholders in the wake of a 1983 bank shares crash.
After the government re-floated shares in Leumi and Bank Hapoalim, Israel's two largest banks, in 1993, the bank privatisation programme almost ground to a halt.

Last month, the government floated about $35 million worth of shares in Israel Discount Bank, the No. 3 bank, in an offering that was nine times oversubscribed and sold 9 percent above the minimum price.

In February, the government re-opened the tender for a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim, Israel's biggest bank, after two bidding groups signalled that they would compete. The government hopes to complete the sale by August.
Less than a year ago, the Hapoalim sale was virtually dead after one of two bidders dropped out, citing red tape.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government plans to raise almost $1 billion for this year's budget from privatising banks and other state-owned companies.
In March, the government sold a block of Israel Chemicals Ltd to the Israel Corp., and it hopes to float shares in Bezeq Israel Telecom in July.
Next week's offering in Leumi will be for units priced at 10 shekels ($2.94) each and containing two ordinary shares and two warrants, the underwriters said.

Each of the warrants will entitle holders to one ordinary share. The series three warrants will come due on Dec. 10, 1997 at a conversion price of 5.15 shekels ($1.50) and the series four on Aug. 10, 1998 at a price of 5.51 shekels ($1.75). The conversion prices are linked to the dollar exchange rate.
The lead underwriters are Israeli brokerages Analyst, IBI and Leader.
